_comment: Hand-written raw-spec.json, used by checks.resolve-import-lazy-lock's #49 case: exercises
classification 8's *non*-firing path -- the spec itself lists lazy.nvim, so lazy-lock.json's
own "lazy.nvim" entry is a genuine match instead of the default hands-off case
lazy.nvim here must not carry `commit` (that closes seedable()'s first early return,
classification 2) and must not carry a `branch` other than "main" (that closes its second,
classification 3) -- either would keep resolvedRef null instead of seeding lazy-lock.json's
own commit for it. `version` is likewise omitted entirely: this check deliberately has
neither git nor --lazy on its PATH/argv (see its own header comment), so any unresolved
version constraint would make the whole run fail outright rather than proving anything about
plain.nvim is the one ordinary plugin: it matches lazy-lock.json's own
{ "commit": "7777..." } entry (no `branch`, no `version`), so "import: N pinned" counts two
-- proving lazy.nvim really is counted alongside a normal seed rather than being the only
